verdicts.text: For Python Pulumi programs, the presence of a `__main__.py` or `setup.py` file defines the entrypoint.
verdicts.evidence: The Python exec shim in pulumi/pulumi (sdk/python/cmd/pulumi-language-python-exec) runs the program with `runpy.run_path(args.PROGRAM, run_name="__main__")` and resolves an extensionless path via `os.path.join(path, "__main__")`. So for a directory the entrypoint is `__main__.py`. I found no `setup.py` handling in that shim. The language host main.go was too large to read past its header.
verdicts.intuition_flag: `setup.py` is a packaging file and doesn't normally define a runnable entrypoint.

verdicts.text: Secret values are decrypted and made available in plain text to the program at runtime, and can be read using any of the standard `pulumi.Config` getters, though using the non-secret getters for a secret is not recommended since it does not mark transitive uses as secret.
verdicts.evidence: In pulumi/pulumi sdk/nodejs/config.ts, `get` returns the raw decrypted string from `getConfig(fullKey)` without secret marking. The secret-warning is commented out ("Temporarily disabling the new warning"). `getSecret` wraps the value with `makeSecret(v)`, so only the secret getters mark it as secret. That supports the claim's core points: secrets are readable as plain text, non-secret getters work, and they don't propagate secretness.
